facts.statement: The species Lagenanectes richterae was described by Sachs, Hornung, and Kear in 2017.
facts.quote:
genus: Lagenanectes
species: richterae
authority: Sachs, Hornung & Kear, 2017

facts.statement: Lagenanectes is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the Lower Cretaceous found in Lower Saxony, Germany.
facts.quote: Lagenanectes is a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur from the Lower Cretaceous, found in Lower Saxony, Germany.

facts.statement: The estimated length of Lagenanectes richterae is about 8 meters (26 feet).
facts.quote: A length of about 8 meters (26 feet) has been estimated.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Lagenanectes richterae was found in 1964 by private collectors in a clay pit near Sarstedt.
facts.quote: The well-preserved holotype specimen of Lagenanectes richterae (specimen number BGR Ma 13328) was found in the disused Moorberg clay pit near Sarstedt by private collectors in 1964.

facts.statement: The age of Lagenanectes fossils is most probably the upper Hauterivian, though it might range from the lower Hauterivian to lower Barremian.
facts.quote: The exact horizon is unknown (the age of the fossils might be lower Hauterivian to lower Barremian, but most probably is upper Hauterivian).

facts.statement: Sven Sachs, Jahn J. Hornung, and Benjamin P. Kear erected the genus Lagenanectes in 2017 after studying the fossil in detail.
facts.quote: However, it was not until some 50 years later, in 2017, that Sven Sachs, Jahn J. Hornung and Benjamin P. Kear studied the fossil in detail and erected Lagenanectes as a new, monotypic genus.

facts.statement: The name Lagenanectes means "Leine swimmer," referring to the Leine river and the animal's swimming lifestyle.
facts.quote: The name Lagenanectes literally means "Leine swimmer" and refers to both, the Leine river which passes Sarstedt, and to the swimming life style of this marine reptile.

facts.statement: The specific name richterae honors Annette Richter for her contributions to paleontological exploration in Lower Saxony.
facts.quote: The specific name richterae honours Annette Richter, chief curator of the Natural History department at the Lower Saxony State Museum in Hannover, for her contributions to the palaeontological exploration of Lower Saxony.

facts.statement: The holotype of Lagenanectes richterae was a fully grown individual, indicated by the ossification of cranial bones, vertebrae, and neural arches.
facts.quote: The holotype of Lagenanectes richterae was a fully grown individual. This is indicated by the ossification of both the cranial bones and the vertebrae and neural arches.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Lagenanectes richterae has unique features including sidewards alveols and a platform with prominent dents on the underside.
facts.quote: The front part of the lower jaw of Lagenanectes richterae shows some anatomical features which are unique in plesiosaurs (autapomorphies): The alveols are placed sidewards and a platform is present on the underside of the lower jaw that bears prominent dents.

facts.statement: Grooves on the upper side of the Lagenanectes skull may have accommodated electroreceptors used to locate prey.
facts.quote: The skull of Lagenanectes shows a rounded snout that is accompanied by some grooves on the upper side. These grooves may have accommodated electroreceptors to locate the prey.

facts.statement: Research demonstrated that Lagenanectes richterae was an early member of the elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: The study by Sachs and colleagues demonstrated that Lagenanectes richterae was an early member of the elasmosaurids.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Lagenanectes in a polytomy with an undescribed plesiosaur from the Speeton Clay and Callawayasaurus.
facts.quote: Following their cladistic analysis, Lagenanectes was in a polytomy with the "Speeton Clay plesiosaur" (a yet undescribed plesiosaur from the Hauterivian of England) and with Callawayasaurus from the Aptian of Colombia.

facts.statement: Pathological alterations in the occiput and first neck vertebra of Lagenanectes richterae may have been caused by an infection.
facts.quote: The occiput and the first neck vertebra of the holotype of Lagenanectes richterae show pathological alterations of the bony structure. They may have been caused by an infection.

facts.statement: Lagenanectes lived between 132.6 and 125.77 million years ago during the Hauterivian.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Hauterivian (132.6 to 125.77 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Lagenanectes richterae is regarded as one of the best-preserved plesiosaur fossils from the Lower Cretaceous in Europe.
rejected.quote: The only species, Lagenanectes richterae, was first described in 2017, and is regarded as one of the best-preserved plesiosaur fossils from this geological age in Europe.
